children: South Korea's headline inflation remained above the central bank's 2% target in October, although it eased from the previous month, potentially reinforcing the case for further monetary policy tightening.

The Bank of Korea will weigh the data closely ahead of a decision later this month when policymakers will consider whether to raise interest rates to curb price pressures stemming from elevated energy costs and strong economic growth.
The benchmark consumer-price index rose 2.8% in October from a year earlier, compared with a 2.9% increase in September, the Ministry of Data and Statistics said Tuesday.
The latest reading was exactly in line with the median forecast of a Wall Street Journal survey of nine economists.
On a month-on-month basis, consumer prices rose 0.2% in October, also matching the survey's forecast. They edged up 0.3% in September.
Core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, rose 2.8% on year in October and gained 0.4% on month.

Fuel costs remained elevated during the month, with gasoline and diesel prices rising 12% and 20%, respectively, from a year earlier. Prices of some industrial goods, including smartphones and computers, also rose sharply while agricultural product prices fell significantly following the country's Chuseok holiday.

Higher global oil prices stemming from the prolonged Middle East conflict have added to inflationary pressures in South Korea, which relies heavily on imported energy. Policymakers are watching for signs that elevated energy costs are spreading to other goods and services, raising the risk of more entrenched inflation.

The BOK held its benchmark interest rate steady at 3.00% last month after raising it at consecutive meetings in July and August. It signaled that further increases could be needed as inflation remained above target and economic growth stayed strong.
South Korea's economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter, expanding 1.0% from the previous quarter, following 0.6% growth in April-June.

Soaring global investment in artificial intelligence and strong semiconductor exports have fueled the recovery in South Korea, home to the world's two largest memory-chip makers. Domestic consumption has also shown signs of improvement, adding to concerns that stronger demand could fuel broader price increases.

For 2026, the BOK expects gross domestic product growth to significantly exceed its August forecast of 3.3%, while projecting headline and core inflation to average 2.7% and 2.5%, respectively, broadly in line with its earlier estimates.
